Bug_Title: Custom serialization methods should have required signatures
Bug_Details:
Java offers a built-in serialization mechanism for classes that implement the Serializable interface. The developer can either rely on
Java’s default serialization and deserialization logic or implement custom methods for these tasks. The JVM will use methods such as readObject and writeObject to execute custom behavior. This only works, however, if these methods match exactly the expected
signatures. If they do not, the JVM will fall back to the default logic, resulting in unexpected behavior at runtime, while the developer believes
that the default logic has been overidden.
This rule raises an issue if an implementation of writeObject , readObject , readObjectNoData , writeReplace , or readResolve has an incorrect access modifier, return type, or is not static when it should be (and
vice-versa).
Bug_Explanation: The bug is that the custom serialization methods writeObject and readObject are not public, so the JVM will fall back to the default serialization logic, causing unexpected behavior at runtime.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the custom serialization methods are not public, causing the JVM to fall back to the default serialization logic, resulting in unexpected behavior at runtime.
